description_md:
## Problem

Sales, stock, purchasing, and finance were tracked separately, so recorded inventory often differed from physical stock. Price changes and purchase costs were difficult to trace, which affected cost of goods sold and inventory valuation. Owners also lacked a single report for reviewing the business.

## Role & constraints

I built the full stack solo as a personal project from October to November 2026. The code is public. I wrote the backend, Vue frontend, and PostgreSQL schema.

## Approach

The application brings sales, products, inventory, suppliers, and purchasing into one system. It generates EAN-13 barcodes and product labels, keeps price history with scheduled and bulk updates, and handles stock opname through physical counts, approval, and adjustment. Inventory value and cost of goods sold use moving weighted average cost, which also feeds gross-profit and margin reports. JWT authentication and role-based access separate ADMIN, OWNER, and CASHIER permissions.

## Result

The system has 18 business features across 15 API route groups. Sales, purchase receipts, returns, and adjustments update stock, and an audit log records each change.

## Lessons

Keeping stock consistent across sales, purchases, returns, and adjustments required careful handling because each operation affects the others. Stock opname also needs separate counting and approval steps to prevent a second approval when two people count at once.
summary: Retail POS for sales, inventory, purchasing, and finance, with moving-average costing and stock-count approvals.
title: Retail Point of Sale (POS) System

description_md:
## Problem

Small restaurants and cafes often handle orders, kitchen updates, and stock separately. Orders reach the kitchen on paper, ingredient levels are estimated at closing, and sales and costs are recorded by hand.

## Role & constraints

I built the full stack solo as a personal project in November 2026. The code is public. I handled the backend, frontend, database, and deployment.

## Approach

A Go backend provides a REST API and server-sent events stream. The React frontend has cashier, kitchen-display, and admin views, backed by PostgreSQL 16. Confirming an order updates ingredient stock, creates the kitchen order, and marks the table occupied in one database transaction. The kitchen display receives outlet-specific updates over SSE. Requests that affect payments or stock use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate processing. The backend checks permissions and denies access by default.

## Result

The system runs on one VPS behind Nginx, with scheduled encrypted backups and an append-only audit log.

## Lessons

Order confirmation locks stock rows in a fixed order within one transaction. I chose a modular monolith over separate services because this project did not need the operational overhead on a single small server.
summary: Restaurant POS with cashier and kitchen screens, table and recipe management, ingredient tracking, shifts, and reports.
title: Food and Beverage POS (Restaurant & Cafe)

description_md:
## Problem

The app's earlier workflow was difficult to follow. It lacked a way to request an extra FAT pole, verify sales visits, or confirm customer identities, leaving reported data unchecked.

## Role & constraints

I worked solo on the backend, Flutter app, PostgreSQL schema, and computer-vision model for my final-year thesis from March to August 2026. The code is private.

## Approach

I added OTP checks for customers and a YOLO26 and PaddleOCR module to read visit evidence. The app also gained a request flow for extra FAT poles and a redesigned Flutter interface. FastAPI serves the API, PostgreSQL stores the data, and Redis caches frequently requested reads.

## Result

The system verifies visits and confirms customers by OTP, reducing manual spot-checks. I handled the backend, frontend, and computer-vision model in one project.
summary: FastAPI and computer-vision system for checking FTTH sales data, verifying visits, and confirming customers by OTP.
title: Computer Vision for FTTH Sales Data Validation

description_md:
## Problem

Material records from raw stock to finished goods were spread across tools. Batch locations were hard to track, some movements went unrecorded, and staff checked Bea Cukai documents by hand. Delivery notes were also manual, fleet locations were unclear, and finance had no production data for costing.

## Role & constraints

I worked on the full stack with a team of three during a freelance engagement from January to April 2026. The code is private.

## Approach

The platform connects production, inventory, distribution, and finance. It records material movements, validates data against the Bea Cukai format through the Customs API, and generates delivery notes. A mobile app tracks containers and vehicles, while production and logistics data feed the finance module for costing and period reports.

## Result

Staff can trace materials through production, validate customs data before submission, and use shared production data for finance instead of re-entering it manually.

## Lessons

The Bea Cukai API required exact data formatting. Warehouse records must pass validation before submission for the customs document to be accepted.
summary: Mini-ERP for tracking materials from production to warehouse, with customs-data validation and finance tools.
title: Integrated Mini-ERP and Logistics Management System

description_md:
## Problem

Sales teams had limited visibility into field visits, and managers could not verify whether a reported visit had taken place.

## Role & constraints

I worked as a backend developer on a team of four during my internship at PT Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, from August to December 2025. The code is private.

## Approach

Sales staff log visits in the app, where an AI model checks the visit evidence. I built the visit and reporting endpoints and stored the data in PostgreSQL.

## Result

Visit reports are generated from recorded activity and checked against visit evidence. The system was used by 100 to 500 members of the sales team.
summary: Field-sales monitoring system that uses AI to check reported visits against visit evidence.
title: DSE AI — Field Sales Activity Monitoring

description_md:
## Problem

Sales staff sometimes missed or forgot visits, while managers lacked live activity updates and prepared daily reports by hand.

## Role & constraints

I worked as a backend developer on a team of seven during my internship from August to December 2025. The code is private.

## Approach

The system schedules visits on Google Maps, groups work areas by village, and supports paired routes. A dashboard turns recorded activity into daily reports for managers.

## Result

Managers can review area performance from the dashboard, and sales staff can plan visits there. The system was used by 200 to 500 members of the sales team.
summary: Sales visit scheduling on Google Maps with a daily-report dashboard for managers.
title: Elang HUB — Sales Visit Scheduling and Reporting

description_md:
## Problem

Managers received the daily report on WhatsApp through a manual process and wanted a way to ask questions about its data.

## Role & constraints

I handled the backend and automation solo on a freelance engagement from August to December 2025. The code is private.

## Approach

I automated the afternoon report delivery to WhatsApp and built a chatbot to answer questions using the same report data. Access is limited to an approved list of phone numbers. The workflows run on n8n, query PostgreSQL, and use KNIME for analysis.

## Result

Managers used the reports and chatbot for two to three months to check area performance without waiting for a manual recap.

## Lessons

Meta requires users to opt in before a business can message them, so the bot only sends reports to an approved audience.
summary: Automated WhatsApp and Telegram reports with a chatbot for managers' questions about sales performance.
title: Chatbot & Daily-Report Automation (WhatsApp/Telegram)

description_md:
## Problem

Water-quality predictions against Indonesian Ministry of Health indicators were not automated, and the dataset was too large to process manually.

## Role & constraints

I worked on data science with one teammate for a course project from June to July 2025. The code is private.

## Approach

I built a PySpark pipeline to clean and prepare more than 1.2 million rows, including handling anomalous values, filling nulls, and reshaping features. A logistic-regression classifier in Spark MLlib predicts whether a sample is safe to drink. I evaluated it using accuracy and AUC.

## Result

The model reached 88.62% accuracy and 0.86 AUC. The pipeline can be run again, rather than relying on a one-off notebook.

## Lessons

Data cleaning took much of the work. At this scale, errors in feature handling can affect the results.
summary: PySpark pipeline that predicts drinking-water safety from more than 1.2 million rows using Indonesian health-ministry indicators.
title: Big Data Predictive Analysis of Drinking-Water Quality

description_md:
## Problem

Campus letters used fixed Microsoft Word templates, while signatures were handled on paper.

## Role & constraints

I worked as a backend developer on a team of eight for a course project from June 2024 to January 2025. The code is private.

## Approach

The system creates official letters from templates, lets administrators track requests across departments, and routes approvals online to the central administration.

## Result

Letter creation time fell from 10 minutes to 2 minutes. Staff can access letters outside the office.

## Lessons

Collecting the correct templates from each department took more effort than expected. The workflow also had to account for paper signatures that are scanned after signing.
summary: Campus letter system with document templates, administrative tracking, and online approvals.
title: SIRATA — Integrated Campus Letter System

description_md:
## Problem

Event organisers needed a way to promote events and sell tickets. Visitors had to find event details and purchasing information across separate channels.

## Role & constraints

I built the backend and event pages as part of a four-person team for a competition from July to August 2024. The code is public.

## Approach

Organisers can publish events and sell tickets. Visitors can browse events, review prices and purchase details, then buy tickets through the platform.

## Result

Organisers can publish events and sell tickets from one platform, where visitors can also find event and purchase information.

## Lessons

Reviewing how ticketing systems handle capacity and payments before development helped avoid rework.
summary: Event platform where organisers publish events and sell tickets, and users can browse and purchase them.
title: Campevent — Event and Ticketing Platform
